title: AMD Reports Tuesday. Here's the Number That Will Show Whether It's Gaining on Nvidia
detail:
AMD Reports Tuesday. Here's the Number That Will Show Whether It's Gaining on Nvidia

Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) is scheduled to report third-quarter results after the market closes on Tuesday, and the stock is heading in on a shaky note. Shares fell nearly 11% on Friday and sold off further on Monday amid broader chip stock weakness, with no AMD-specific news. In all, AMD is down nearly 30% from its all-time high, reached less than a month ago.

Of course, we have no idea what AMD will report, but the headline results probably won't be the surprise. AMD guided for revenue of about $13 billion, plus or minus $300 million, and analysts expect $13.09 billion, which would be 41.5% higher than a year ago.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

The guidance is the real story

The more important figure is likely to be AMD's fourth-quarter guidance, and specifically how much of it comes from data center GPUs. AMD began shipping its Helios rack-scale systems, built on its MI450 chips, in September, so the third quarter won't include a full period of its volume. However, management said on its last call that it expects the ramp to accelerate meaningfully in the fourth quarter.

The average estimate among Wall Street analysts is about $16.3 billion in fourth-quarter revenue, and Jefferies analyst Blayne Curtis expects closer to $17 billion. A forecast at or above that higher level would suggest Helios demand is turning into revenue at an impressive pace. AMD has plenty of big customers lined up, including OpenAI, Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META), Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT), and Anthropic, so expectations are high.

AMD doesn't need to catch Nvidia

To put AMD's AI business in perspective, Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) generated $89 billion of data center revenue in its most recent quarter. AMD's entire data center segment, which includes its EPYC server processors, generated $6.7 billion in revenue. AMD isn't going to close that gap anytime soon.

However, it doesn't need to. AI companies want a second source of computing power so they aren't completely dependent on one supplier, and AMD has emerged as the most credible alternative. CEO Lisa Su has said each gigawatt of AI capacity represents double-digit billions in revenue, so even a modest share of the market would be an enormous win.

Of course, there are risks to watch. For example, AI chips carry slightly lower margins than server processors, so a fast GPU ramp could weigh on gross margin. It's also worth noting that Intel's (NASDAQ:INTC) warning about a shrinking PC market could also be a headwind for AMD's client business, which grew 23% last quarter.

Still riding the positive momentum from a satisfying quarterly earnings report, Capri Holdings (NYSE:CPRI) stock cruised to a more than 7% gain on Monday. Also providing plenty of fuel for this was a set of analyst price target increases on the fashion conglomerate's stock.

A company in style for the market

Capri's second quarter of fiscal 2027 results were published Friday morning. Although revenue declined by almost 6% year over year to $809 million, the company flipped to a non-GAAP (adjusted) net income of $45 million. On top of that, it obliterated analyst profitability estimates and comfortably beat on the top line.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

On Monday, analysts tracking the stock reacted overwhelmingly positively to the consumer discretionary company's performance. Several expressed this by raising their Capri price targets.

Among these was Brooke Roach from the ever-influential investment bank Goldman Sachs (NYSE:GS). She lifted hers to $24 from $18, albeit while maintaining her neutral recommendation. A more bullish note was authored by Barclays' (NYSE:BCS) Adrienne Yih, who now feels the stock is worth $24 apiece, up from her preceding $19. She kept her overweight (i.e., buy) recommendation intact.

A tale of two fashion lines

I'm always rather hesitant about fashion stocks, as they're subject to trends, whims, and the health of the economy. That said, Capri's Jimmy Choo line did especially well and looks set to continue doing so, even if the larger Michael Kors unit is currently in turnaround mode. Meanwhile, management is effectively trimming costs behind the scenes. If I were to consider buying any fashion title, I'd certainly add this one to the list.

The maker of graphics chips for gaming and artificial intelligence's shares have seen a decrease of 12.53% over the last month, not keeping up with the Computer and Technology sector's loss of 9.88% and the S&P 500's loss of 0.87%.

Market participants will be closely following the financial results of Nvidia in its upcoming release. The company plans to announce its earnings on November 17, 2026. The company's upcoming EPS is projected at $2.49, signifying a 91.54% increase compared to the same quarter of the previous year. Meanwhile, the latest consensus estimate predicts the revenue to be $108.99 billion, indicating a 91.19% increase compared to the same quarter of the previous year.

For the entire fiscal year, the Zacks Consensus Estimates are projecting earnings of $9.3 per share and a revenue of $407.51 billion, representing changes of +94.97% and +88.72%, respectively, from the prior year.

Any recent changes to analyst estimates for Nvidia should also be noted by investors. These latest adjustments often mirror the shifting dynamics of short-term business patterns. With this in mind, we can consider positive estimate revisions a sign of optimism about the business outlook.

Empirical research indicates that these revisions in estimates have a direct correlation with impending stock price performance. We developed the Zacks Rank to capitalize on this phenomenon. Our system takes these estimate changes into account and delivers a clear, actionable rating model.

The Zacks Rank system, stretching from #1 (Strong Buy) to #5 (Strong Sell), has a noteworthy track record of outperforming, validated by third-party audits, with stocks rated #1 producing an average annual return of +25% since the year 1988. Over the past month, there's been a 0.56% rise in the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. Nvidia currently has a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy).

Looking at valuation, Nvidia is presently trading at a Forward P/E ratio of 22.01. For comparison, its industry has an average Forward P/E of 27.92, which means Nvidia is trading at a discount to the group.

We can additionally observe that NVDA currently boasts a PEG ratio of 1.57. The PEG ratio is akin to the commonly utilized P/E ratio, but this measure also incorporates the company's anticipated earnings growth rate. NVDA's industry had an average PEG ratio of 1.57 as of yesterday's close.
